notes:
Passed on the fake backend by python3 -m mhs.driver check (evidence contract_checked; simulated R0, model-authored and unreviewed; no hardware run and no MHS-Device level claimed). The clone has no fixed env_id: ArenaEnvBuilder.build_registered takes the id from self.arena_env.name and calls gym.register(id=name), so a composed IsaacLabArenaEnvironment must be built first; the Gymnasium family's gym.make(env_id) path is therefore not configured and this package provides only the package fake backend. The upstream stack (Isaac Sim 6.1, Isaac Lab 3.0, Python 3.12, Linux, NVIDIA GPU) was never started here. The fake is a one-coordinate kinematic F0 stand-in: the real action space is the batched Box of Isaac Lab's action manager (width = sum of the action term dimensions, chosen by the composed embodiment) and the real observation is a Dict of observation groups, while the fake uses a one-element action Box and one policy group; the upstream environment is vectorized over num_envs and the MHS Gymnasium bridge drives one environment. These reductions are in fidelity.gaps. Warnings are explained: G6.NO_NATIVE_CALL for cap.world.seed.v1 is expected (the seed only sets the next reset); G7.MAYBE_ABSENT for action_space and observation_space is expected because the native class inherits them from ManagerBasedRLEnv outside the clone; the four G8.NO_UNIT warnings are the bridge-derived integer and action inputs; G8.SAFE014_NOT_APPLICABLE is truthful because the upstream action Box is unbounded and no finite action bound can be sourced, so SAFE-014 has nothing to probe and the suite awards CL2 instead of CL3. There are no G4.REF_VALUE or G4.REF_BINARY warnings. No catalogue requests: only cap.world.step.v1, cap.world.reset.v1 and cap.world.seed.v1 are used. check-report.json is regenerated by every gate run and is not part of the package.
